size.note: Newman's Birds gives 28–30 cm and 100–200 g.

habitat: Flocks, often hundreds, in grassland and Karoo, perched on posts, pylons, wires or bushes. Roosts in tall trees, usually Eucalyptus.
summary: An uncommon to locally common summer visitor. Both sexes have rufous upperwings. The male has a grey head, grey secondary coverts, a grey back and a grey upper tail, plain underwings and a plain mantle. The female is more slender than a Rock Kestrel, paler below than above, with a brown tail barred black. Newman does not describe the voice. Months were left unset. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Rock Kestrel lacks the contrast between upper parts and underparts, is more robust, and has a grey tail. Female Lesser Kestrel has a brown tail barred black.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

upperparts.pattern: Plain mantle, not spotted. Grey secondary coverts.

wings.pattern: Rufous upperwings, with grey upper wing coverts. Plain underwings.

viewNotes.note: Rufous upperwings, a grey head and a plain mantle.
Grey head. The underparts were not given a separate colour beyond the plain underwings.
Grey back and grey upper tail.
Plain underwings and grey upper wing coverts. Flocks wheel in leisurely flight.

calls.description: Newman’s species page does not describe the voice. Grade A call from Ávila, Spain. The filename is Rodfalk, the Swedish name.
